clue.text: Heard dog barking somewhere in Ireland

definitions.note: a town on the Boyne in County Louth

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of heard and dog are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noisy dog is heard yapping somewhere on the Irish countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dog's noise but means mad, the anagram signal for HEARD DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A port town in County Louth, Ireland, famous for Cromwell's siege, so it is a place in Ireland.

clue.text: Leaves fools, possibly half-heartedly

indicators.note: losing half of the heart: one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, so fools are an example of sweets served after the main course

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the foolish, if only without full commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of puréed fruit and cream; DESSERTS has SS at its heart, and 'half-heartedly' removes one S.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone in the lurch is to abandon them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Squash ego, getting Andrea in a tizzy

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of agitation, so the letters of ego and Andrea are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone deflates an ego by sending Andrea into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' reads as a verb (crush an ego) but is the noun, a fruit drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain squash is a fruit cordial diluted with water, and this fizzy citrus drink is such a soft drink.

clue.text: For the time being, covers Spurs at home

definitions.note: a verb phrase: temporarily buries plant roots

parts.note: to spur a horse is to urge it on with the heels, so spurs means heels as a verb
at home means in

explanation.surface: A sports fan reports Tottenham (Spurs) playing at home, covered for now.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club, a distraction here. To heel in is a gardening term: to plant roots temporarily in a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners temporarily bury the roots of plants in soil until permanent planting, which is a temporary covering.

clue.text: Duke using several points to stifle start of pay increases

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the points surround the next letter

parts.note: E, E, E, N and S are compass points

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A duke uses compass bearings to suppress the beginnings of pay rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stifle' puts P inside the string of compass points EEENS, giving EEPENS after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To make deeper is to intensify or grow, so the verb means increases.

clue.text: Fancy one possibly single girl who's interrupting question

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of something, so these letters go inside

parts.note: why is a question
I is the Roman numeral one
Ms is the title for a woman who may be unmarried

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a single girl who keeps cutting into a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb (to fancy a girl) but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim or playful notion is a fancy, the noun sense of imaginative caprice.

clue.text: Private doctor sporting a beard when doing the rounds?

indicators.note: going around something, so the bearded phrase encloses the doctor

parts.note: sporting a beard is being with one
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley

explanation.surface: A bearded doctor making ward rounds in private practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the rounds' suggests a doctor's ward visits but here means going around the doctor. An awn is the bristle, or beard, on an ear of barley.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, retiring person who keeps to themselves is described as being shy and uncommunicative.

clue.text: I go under, making retraction about a summing up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word a goes inside
a retraction draws back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to drown is to go under water

explanation.surface: Someone admits to failing and withdraws a remark about a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside DROWN to give DROWAN, which 'making retraction' turns into NAWORD after I.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a brief summary, so it means briefly or in short.

clue.text: Type of home cooking served first?

definitions.meaning: a first home bought by a young buyer is so called
the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: A kind of home-style cooking that is brought out ahead of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: A starter home is a small first house; a starter is the opening course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe a beginning: the first course of dinner and a first-time buyer's house.

clue.text: Carnivore for whom siesta came unexpectedly

indicators.note: something unexpected arrives in an unforeseen form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A meat-eater who was surprised when the afternoon nap arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: This pedigree feline from Thailand eats meat, an example of a flesh-eating animal.

clue.text: Hero, briefly, not to cross

definitions.note: the Greek warrior of the Trojan War

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a door that is to is closed, so one not to is slightly open, ajar
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A hero is told, in a word, not to get angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is an old sense of a door pushed shut ('pull the door to'), so 'not to' means ajar; 'briefly' docks its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The mighty Greek warrior at Troy who fought Hector is a legendary hero of the Iliad.

clue.text: Entered after sign for this?

definitions.note: a noun phrase: mail you sign for on delivery

parts.note: entered in a record means registered
post means after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: Someone writes a name in a book after signing for a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: Post as a Latin prefix means after. 'Entered' is the past tense, not someone coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Mail's recorded, insured delivery requires the recipient's signature on arrival.

clue.text: In report, spots in which Surrey homes have been built

definitions.text: in which Surrey homes have been built

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: spots and marks are stains

explanation.surface: A survey report on blemishes found in new houses in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines-upon-Thames is a town in Surrey, near Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: This Thames-side town lies in Surrey, so it is a place where Surrey houses stand.

clue.text: Praised Brussels journalist keeping watch on US troops

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the watch word comes before the soldiers

parts.note: lo means look or behold
GIs are American soldiers
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An EU-based reporter who keeps an eye on American soldiers heaps praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo is an old word meaning look; GIs are American soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a formal speech of praise, often at a funeral, is to extol someone.

clue.text: Possible definition of loutish behaviour with tears

definitions.meaning: read as lad plus -ery, the conduct of a boorish young man
tights with runs or rips in them

explanation.surface: A dictionary editor suggests a meaning for yobbish conduct ending in weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is a British word for a run in tights; a lad is a boisterous young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery that is laddered has runs, the British word for tears in stockings.

clue.text: Stop press — leaves to go in as an afterthought

definitions.text: leaves to go in as an afterthought

parts.note: to stop is to end
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: A newspaper's late news column holds back items and inserts them at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop press' is late news added to a printed paper; here the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Blank sheets bound into a book's covers after the text is printed are pages added as finishing leaves.

clue.text: Settler somehow providing support

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pioneer manages, one way or another, to give help.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of legs with a crossbar holds up a table top, so it is a kind of prop.

clue.text: Whip concealed in drawer removed from case

indicators.note: in places the hidden word inside the other letters
the outer letters, the case, are stripped from the word drawer

parts.note: concealed means hid, kept out of sight

explanation.surface: A whip was hidden in a drawer and then taken out of its box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from case' strips the outer letters of DRAWER; 'in' then puts the past tense of hide inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip of untanned leather, as used by cowboys, is a type of lash.

clue.text: Wise to have Liberal for President, initially outstanding

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: sapient means wise

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A wise politician has a Liberal installed as President and is an early success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps L in place of P, the initial of President, in SAPIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sticks out or is most noticeable is prominent, the sense of standing out.

clue.text: One who won't fight to stop over as secrets are dispatched?

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so the objector sits inside

parts.note: over means finished, ended
CO is a conscientious objector

explanation.surface: A pacifist intervenes to halt a stopover while classified papers are sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: CO, conscientious objector, is a crossword staple; 'to stop' means to plug, so it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret messages are sent in cipher, put into code before transmission.

clue.text: Unexpectedly learn about Poles put into difficulty?

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the poles
unexpectedly means in an unforeseen way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find out about Polish people in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' with a capital looks like nationality but means the north and south poles; 'Unexpectedly' makes ENARL, and 'about' puts them inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle someone is to catch them in a snare, putting them in a tight spot.

clue.text: Perhaps cast judge out from manoeuvre in church

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: out from means taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to jockey for position is to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A judge is thrown out of manoeuvres inside a church, perhaps a cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' is an eye defect, not actors; 'out from' leaves OCKEY, which 'in' places inside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast in the eye is a squint, and a squinting eye is an example.

clue.text: Porcelain that was notoriously fired

definitions.meaning: fine Meissen china is sold under this city's name
the German city firebombed by the Allies in 1945

explanation.walkthrough: Porcelain is fired in a kiln; the city was set ablaze in the bombing raids of February 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxon porcelain from Meissen is known by the city's name, and the city was infamously firebombed.

clue.text: Perhaps going after Canada is a waste of time

definitions.meaning: hunting a Canada, a species of untamed waterfowl

explanation.surface: Pursuing a career in Canada might prove fruitless.
explanation.walkthrough: A Canada is a species of goose, so going after one is pursuing a wild bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a hopeless, pointless pursuit that achieves nothing.

clue.text: Extra roomy

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach scores an extra run

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat; a ball bowled out of reach is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious means broad, and in cricket the term names one type of extra run.

clue.text: Oil producer having word with open tennis star?

parts.note: open sesame is the magic phrase from Ali Baba
a top-ranked player in a tournament draw is a seed

explanation.surface: A tennis star at an open championship has a word with an oil tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open sesame' opens the cave in Ali Baba; a seed is a top-ranked tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: This small kernel is pressed to make a cooking oil, so it is a source of oil.

clue.text: Seven Samurai maybe needing leader to accept point

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the leader surrounds the point

parts.note: a head is a leader

explanation.surface: Kurosawa's band of warriors needs a chief who will take a point.
explanation.walkthrough: The film Seven Samurai is an example of a group of seven, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven is so named from Greek, and the film's seven swordsmen form one.

clue.text: Old copper returns to stop second offence and ignores alarm?

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so the reversed word goes inside

parts.note: a sin is an offence

indicators.note: returns means going back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: peelers were early policemen, after Robert Peel who founded the force

explanation.surface: A former policeman returns to prevent a second crime, ignoring the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robert Peel founded the Metropolitan Police, whose officers were called peelers; 'returns' gives LEEP, which 'to stop' sets inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed past the usual time means disregarding the morning clock's ring.
